_doc: Each section offers three cards: q=2 strong, q=1 okay, q=0 weak. 'type' is the short line the player types. {subject} is replaced by the assignment topic.

sections.title: Thesis
sections.hint: One clear claim you can actually defend.

cards.text: There are many views on {subject}, and this essay will look at some of them.
cards.type: There are many views on this topic.

cards.text: This essay argues that {subject} matters because it shapes everyday life in ways that are easy to overlook.
cards.type: This matters because it shapes everyday life.

cards.text: Since the dawn of time, humans have always had opinions about {subject}.
cards.type: Since the dawn of time, humans have opinions.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.hint: Set up the question. Don't write the whole essay here.

cards.text: Begin with one concrete example, then narrow to the question the essay will answer.
Define every word in the title using a dictionary, then repeat the title.
Briefly introduce the topic and list the three points that follow.
cards.type: This essay covers three main points.

sections.title: Evidence
sections.hint: A claim needs something under it.

cards.text: Say that a lot of people agree and move on.
cards.type: A lot of people agree on this.

cards.text: Pick two specific sources or examples and explain exactly how each supports the thesis.
cards.type: The first example supports this because

cards.text: Quote one source and summarise it without connecting it back.
cards.type: One source states that this is true.

cards.text: Restate the thesis and summarise the main points.
cards.type: In conclusion, the main points are clear.

cards.text: Introduce an entirely new argument in the last line.
cards.type: However, there is one more thing.

cards.text: Return to the opening example and show what has changed in how we see it.
cards.type: Seen again, the example looks different.

distractions: Battery at 20%. Plug in the phone?
